name: Meyer Wire & Cable Co
old_description: Meyer Wire & Cable Company LLC, is a designer and manufacturer of quality cable and coil cords.
about:
Meyer Wire & Cable Co. was founded in 1972 by Henry Meyer in Hamden, Connecticut. Originally located the company moved to its current facility in 1975.

The company designs and manufactures custom coil cords and cable assemblies, specializing in highly flexible, durable retractile cords rated for up to 20 million flex cycles. It produces both small custom batches and bulk cable runs (typically 1,000 feet), and offers a coiling service for customer-supplied cable with mandrel diameters from 0.125 to 2.25 inches and retracted lengths up to 96 inches. Value-added services include custom terminations—stripping, tinning, spade terminals, modular connectors, grommets, bands, and strain reliefs—as well as cable design support and in-process quality testing. Lead times for bulk cable are typically under three weeks, and quote requests are answered the same day.

Meyer Wire’s products serve a range of industries requiring flexible interconnect solutions, though the company does not publicly list specific sectors. Its cords are built to meet diverse application requirements, from easy-pull to rugged environments, and all products are RoHS and REACH compliant with UL-listed options available.

The firm emphasizes rapid response and small-run flexibility as key differentiators, rooted in a culture of “wire dedication” spanning three generations. Free coiling of customer-provided cable samples and free cord samples from stock further reduce development risk for clients.

name: Michaelson Foreign & Domestic Car Parts
old_description: Since 1926, Michaelson has been working hard to earn its reputation as New Jersey’s top auto recycler.
about:
Michaelson Foreign & Domestic Car Parts has operated from South River, New Jersey, since 1926. The business was founded by the Michaelson family and began as a community‑focused salvage yard serving local drivers and repair shops. Now approaching its centennial, the company remains family‑owned and continues the tradition started nearly a hundred years ago.

The company functions as an auto recycler, dismantling late‑model foreign and domestic vehicles to harvest reusable parts, glass, and accessories. Its South River facility is described as highly organized and meticulously clean, housing a massive inventory that is searchable online. In addition to walk‑in sales, Michaelson ships nationwide through its own e‑commerce site and an eBay store, offering tested components with fast delivery.

Customers include independent repair shops, collision centers, and individual vehicle owners across the United States who need affordable, recycled replacement parts for both foreign and domestic makes. The firm’s network of nationwide parts resources supplements its own stock, ensuring buyers can locate hard‑to‑find items.

Michaelson emphasizes its long‑standing reputation as New Jersey’s top auto recycler, attributing its longevity to unmatched customer service, a clean and well‑organized yard, and a commitment to keeping the family tradition alive. The company says it evolved from a local operation to a coast‑to‑coast supplier while maintaining the personal touch of a family business.

name: Michigan Milk Producers Association
old_description: Operated by MMPA subsidiary Middlebury Cheese Company LLC, the Middlebury plant specializes in producing barrel and delihorn cheeses sold to wholesale customers and under the
about:
Michigan Milk Producers Association (MMPA) is a dairy cooperative founded in 1916 and headquartered in Novi, Michigan. The member‑owned organization began as a collective of dairy farmers in the Great Lakes region and has grown to operate processing facilities across Michigan, Indiana, and Ohio.

The cooperative runs five dairy processing plants. Its largest facility in Ovid, Michigan, handles more than 5 million pounds of milk per day, producing butter, milk powder, condensed milk, cream, and ultrafiltered milk. A plant in Constantine, Michigan, processes nearly 3 million pounds daily into ultrafiltered milk, cream, and condensed skim milk, with an adjacent ethanol plant that converts dairy byproducts. In Remus, Michigan, a cottage cheese plant processes over 500,000 pounds daily. The Middlebury, Indiana plant, operated through the Middlebury Cheese Company subsidiary, focuses on barrel and delihorn cheeses sold wholesale and under the Heritage Ridge Creamery brand. The Canton, Ohio facility, home to the Superior Dairy and Creative Edge subsidiaries, produces fluid milk and ice cream for national distribution. A farm supply store in Mt. Pleasant serves members and the public.

MMPA sells dairy ingredients to food manufacturers that make salad dressing, infant formula, candy, ice cream, pudding, baked goods, cheese, and yogurt. Its retail brands supply ice cream and fluid milk directly to consumers. The cooperative also provides milk testing and farm supply services to its member farms across Michigan, Indiana, Ohio, and Wisconsin.

The association emphasizes quality and sustainability, noting its Safe Quality Foods certification, Green Agri‑Business designations for the Ovid and Constantine plants, and numerous World Dairy Expo championship awards. Members participate in the National Dairy F.A.R.M. program for animal care, and the cooperative maintains an FDA‑certified central laboratory for milk quality assurance.

name: Micro-Tek Corporation
old_description: Micro-Tek specializes in custom drawing, flattening, stranding and insulating, cutting and stripping of fine wire and cable .0009" (AWG #50) and larger.
about:
Micro-Tek Corporation operates from a 30,000-square-foot facility in Cinnaminson, New Jersey. The company was founded in 1965 by George Rogers as the Miniature Insulated Wire Company and incorporated under its current name in 1966. Now under third-generation family ownership, the business has grown from a small shop into a multi-generational manufacturer serving aerospace, medical, and industrial markets worldwide.

Micro-Tek specializes in custom drawing, flattening, stranding, insulating, cutting, and stripping of fine wire and cable down to .0009 inch (AWG #50). Its capabilities include PTFE fluoropolymer extrusion for coax cores, tubing, and cables; etching for bondability on PTFE, FEP, PFA, and ETFE; wire winding; and contract manufacturing. All processes—wire drawing, stranding, insulating, and tubing—are performed under one roof, supporting custom and short runs as well as high-volume production.

The company serves aerospace customers with micro-coaxial cable, shielded twisted pair cable, and high-performance coaxial core for avionics, satellite systems, and communication equipment. In the medical sector, it supplies PTFE coaxial core, flat wire, fluoropolymer tubing, and etched liners for surgical devices, diagnostic imaging, braiding, coiling, and sensors. Industrial clients use its custom wire and cable for automation systems and high-temperature manufacturing processes requiring chemical resistance and durability.

Micro-Tek emphasizes precision, holding tolerances as fine as ±0.0002 inch, and flexibility, offering small runs, large orders, and just-in-time or contract manufacturing. The company cites its decades of experience, ISO 9001:2015 certification, and long-term customer relationships as key differentiators.

about:
Microchip Auto Glass has operated from Tacoma, Washington since 2010. The company provides mobile auto glass repair and replacement services across the greater Puget Sound region, traveling to customers in cities including Seattle, Bellevue, Olympia, and surrounding communities. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The shop performs windshield replacement for passenger vehicles and semi-trucks, door glass replacement, sunroof replacement, window regulator repair and replacement, and ADAS calibration following glass replacement or collision work. Technicians use what the company describes as state-of-the-art equipment for recalibrating advanced driver assistance systems. Service vehicles carry inventory for on-site installation, and the company notes a courtesy vacuum cleaning step during door glass jobs to remove residual glass from interiors and door cavities.

Customers range from individual vehicle owners to commercial fleets operating Peterbilt, Freightliner, Kenworth, Volvo, International, and Mack trucks. The fleet program emphasizes minimal downtime for businesses with multiple vehicles. The company also serves heavy-duty truck operators requiring windshield replacement that meets sealing and structural standards for long-haul operation.

Microchip Auto Glass distinguishes itself through mobile service delivery, a relatively uncommon focus on regulator and sunroof repairs, and ADAS calibration capability that many general glass shops do not offer. A warranty backs all windshield replacements, and the company highlights its ability to handle both passenger car and Class 8 truck glass work from the same mobile platform.
